claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with hierarchical dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Internal lamellar or colony boundaries in the starting alloy impede dislocation motion.
Warm cyclic pre-straining below the recrystallization temperature can modify the internal colony interfaces.
A sub-critical warm treatment can activate dislocation sources without causing unwanted phase coarsening.
Warm cyclic pre-straining will improve the coherency and connectivity of the lamellar interfaces.
Coherent lamellar interfaces can facilitate dislocation passage across phase boundaries.
Cyclic pre-straining rearranges and pre-activates dislocation sources at internal lamellar boundaries.
The proposed treatment reduces dislocation pile-ups at internal lamellar boundaries.
Improved dislocation transmission across lamellae alleviates local stress concentrations and avoids cracking.
Reducing pile-ups lowers interfacial strain-energy accumulation.
Lower interfacial strain-energy accumulation delays microcrack initiation.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature ductility because dislocation pile-ups create local stress concentrations and premature microcracking.
Warm cyclic pre-straining will significantly increase room-temperature tensile elongation relative to the untreated alloy.
Warm cyclic pre-straining will maintain or slightly increase tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed improvement applies under room-temperature, quasi-static tensile loading.
The improvement may not transfer to high-strain-rate or high-temperature service without adapting the treatment parameters.

contradictions.description: The conditions field initially says that both treatment and testing occur under room-temperature tensile conditions, whereas the intervention and the remainder of the conditions field specify pre-straining at a moderately elevated temperature.
